answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with stake-backed quadratic voting: each identity locks collateral, but voting weight is the square root of the amount locked, so splitting one wallet into a thousand fake agents earns about thirty-two votes, not a thousand. The signal that matters is the bond in escrow, as durable and visible as quartz; an identity caught double-voting is slashed to its nadir and loses the deposit. Influence thus costs an attacker collateral rising with the square of the votes sought, so a Sybil swarm is far pricier than one honest stake.
